b1.summary: All 6 runs kept every functional test (165/165) and failed only security tests. Every run failed the block-based (differential) download redirect tests: the multi-range test and the trailing block-map range test in 6/6, the single-range test in 4/6. Every run also failed both failed-command stdout/stderr redaction tests (6/6). JSON debug/error redaction failed in 5/6, and the header-case variants in 1 MiMo run. Decisive: differential redirect (real upstream code the published fix never touches) and the command-output redaction (a published-fix site).

b2.note: 4 levers fail in every run (multi-range differential, embedded block map, command stderr, command stdout), so no single test decides the breaker. The injected Gitea tests (T5-T7) never failed in any run.

b4.note: Same core in all 6 runs (differential + command output); runs differ only in whether JSON debug/error redaction and the single-range differential test were also missed.

b5.open_human_question: NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES - confirm the in-process fakeElectron stand-in is faithful to Electron 39 for the full-download test, and that the two upgrade-added security tests (full download, embedded trailing range) get the full launcher re-gate, not only the targeted runs in notes.md. Also the review's 'Required: generalize' items were never applied: instruction.md still says 'Private servers keep working.' and 'whether an error message or debug output'.

b6.reason: Upstream fix 22a7532b changes httpExecutor (normalised header-name strip, safeStringifyJson in debug/error text), util.ts (adds privateToken/apiKey stems and runs removePassword on child stdout/stderr) and the GitHub/GitLab publishers. So the command-output, JSON-redaction and header-variant failures are covered. It never touches electron-updater/src/differentialDownloader/*, so the differential/multi-range/embedded-block-map redirect leak is uncovered. That gap fails in every run, so the breaker survives a lookup of the fix (the instruction's 'Do not look up the upstream fix' line could not be enforced in the real setting).

c1.mechanism: credential leak on cross-origin redirect + secret in diagnostic output

c2.pattern: missed indirect route (second redirect path in a separate subsystem)
c2.note: The decisive gap is the updater's block-based download, which re-issues redirects itself (followRedirect / no redirect handler) instead of going through the shared helper the published fix hardens. A secondary decisive trap is a published-fix far site (command stdout/stderr redaction). The injected Gitea publisher was solved in every run.

d2.evidence: giteaPublisher.ts is wired into PublishManager.createPublisher/requireProviderClass with GiteaOptions docs and mirrors the GitHub/GitLab publishers, which is plausible. Two of the three flaws read as placed: the constructor runs log.debug({config: JSON.stringify({..., token: this.token})}, 'Gitea publisher configuration') (a token put into a debug dump by name), and send() hand-rolls a 3xx follow that re-sends Authorization although httpExecutor already has redirect handling. FAIRNESS also notes that a 307 on a Gitea asset PUT is atypical (Gitea uses POST). These sites were never decisive.

e3.why: READY, but NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES is open (fakeElectron fidelity, full re-gate of the upgrade tests), and the required generalize edits were not applied

e4.why: every run leaves the credential reaching the redirect target on the differential download path

e5.why: differential/block-map redirect code is untouched by upstream 22a7532b and fails in 6/6 runs

concerns: Injection contributed nothing: all 6 runs fixed the 3 injected Gitea traps. The breaker rests on real upstream code (differential downloader) and published-fix far sites.
Two of the decisive differential tests (embedded block map, Electron full download) were added in the 2026-10-20 upgrade with targeted runs only; the full launcher re-gate is listed as pending.
The differential tests run against an in-process fakeElectron stand-in; its fidelity to Electron 39 is an open human-review item.
Part of the decisive set (command stdout/stderr, JSON redaction) is covered by the public upstream fix, so an open-internet solver would close those. Only the differential lever survives.
The FAIRNESS 'Required: generalize' edits ('Private servers keep working.', the channel enumeration) are still in instruction.md.
one_line: electron-builder: both models stripped credentials in the shared redirect helper but never found that the updater's block-based (differential) download follows redirects on its own path, and they also missed secrets in failed-command output.
